paper.citation: Dimitriadis, T., Dümbgen, L., Henzi, A., Puke, M. and Ziegel, J. (2023). Honest calibration assessment for binary outcome predictions. Biometrika, 110(3), 663–680. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asac068.
paper.venue: Biometrika (formal publication, 2023); arXiv preprint v2 is the checked DGP version
paper.source_locator: DGP source actually checked in arXiv:2203.04065v2 (2022-11-02), PDF p.8, Section 5, item 2 (S-shaped); X~U[0,1] and Y~Bernoulli{p_s(X)} are specified on the same page. Supplementary Material PDF pp.17–20 covers rounding, application details, and proofs and does not state a changed S-shaped DGP. The paper gives replication URL https://github.com/marius-cp/replication_DDHPZ22 but no fixed code commit. Formal Biometrika DGP differences were not checked.

mechanism.name: S-shaped binary regression functions from Dimitriadis et al. (2023)

generation_equations.label: S-shaped regression function (endpoint-safe equivalent)
generation_equations.expression: p_s(x) = x^(1+s) / (x^(1+s) + (1-x)^(1+s)), with endpoint values 0 and 1

generation_equations.label: NRI scalar target
generation_equations.expression: m_s(0.5) = E[Y | X=0.5] = p_s(0.5) = 0.5 for every declared s

sampling.dependence: iid across observations; no cluster, panel, network, or within-unit dependence

assumptions: Independent and identically distributed individual observations (X_i,Y_i).
X has the source distribution Uniform[0,1] and the fixed query x*=0.5 lies in its support interior.
Given X=x, Y is Bernoulli with success probability p_s(x); at x=0 and x=1 the regression function is defined by the continuous endpoint limits 0 and 1.
For every declared scenario s>=0, p_s is nondecreasing on [0,1] and smooth on (0,1), matching the monotonicity condition used for the source simultaneous-band method.
The scalar truth is evaluated under the known DGP; no causal exchangeability, treatment, mediator, or interference assumption is relevant.

properties.notes: The only covariate is X, so total and effective dimensions are both one. There are no interaction terms. The S-shaped regression function is p_s(x)=x^(1+s)/(x^(1+s)+(1-x)^(1+s)); it is nonlinear for s>0 and reduces to the linear diagonal p_0(x)=x at s=0. The binary outcome link is Bernoulli with this conditional probability. The s=0 case is retained for source fidelity but must be deduplicated against s=0 scenarios from the monomial, kink, or wave templates.

estimand.name: m_s(x*) = E[Y | X=x*] = p_s(x*)
estimand.definition: Noncausal nonparametric regression function at the fixed query x*=0.5 for a selected source scenario s in {0,0.1,...,1}; with p_s(x)=[1+{(1-x)/x}^(1+s)]^(-1), the target is p_s(0.5). This is a conditional Bernoulli probability, not an intervention effect or a prediction interval.

truth.expression: Noncausal nonparametric regression function at the fixed query x*=0.5 for a selected source scenario s in {0,0.1,...,1}; with p_s(x)=[1+{(1-x)/x}^(1+s)]^(-1), the target is p_s(0.5). This is a conditional Bernoulli probability, not an intervention effect or a prediction interval.
truth.derivation: Closed-form stable evaluation at the fixed query p_s(0.5)=0.5 because the two powers are equal; independently checked with the original odds expression and the endpoint/symmetry identities.

adaptations: Register the source shape grid s=0,0.1,...,1 as eleven named scenarios and use s=0.5 as the default; these are source parameter settings, not new mechanism families.
Expose the scalar NRI target p_s(0.5)=E[Y|X=0.5] required by the collection interface. The source studies simultaneous confidence bands over x, not this scalar truth hook.

Implement the algebraically equivalent endpoint-safe formula x^(1+s)/(x^(1+s)+(1-x)^(1+s)) and run the collection smoke check instead of the source's 1000-replication coverage experiment; no confidence band, bootstrap, or coverage result is claimed.
